item.title: No. 13 Oregon uses special teams trickery again to ignite another runaway win, thumps Michigan State
item.description: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning has overseen a midseason turnaround after the Ducks lost three of their first seven games. (AP Photo/Al Goldis) AP Photo/Al Goldis Long before No. 13 Oregon put the finishing touches on its 45-7 dismantling of Michigan State (3-8, 1-7 Big Ten) on Friday night in East Lansing, points were coming at a premium for the Ducks (8-3, 6-2). For the second time in three games, head coach Dan Lanning used special teams trickery to ignite a runaway win. With his team up 10-0 and seven seconds remaining in the second quarter, Lanning opted for a fake field goal on the final play of the first half. Instead of attempting a 33-yard attempt, kicker Gage Hurych received a pitch from his holder and, eventually, a block from tight end Jamari Johnson en route to the end zone. Hurych broke one tackle and crossed the goal line prior to going down. Lanning was elated, as were his coaches and players. The Ducks went on to score touchdowns on four of their first five drives of the second half. Their sixth and final series of the half consisted of a couple kneel downs. IT'S A FAKE! @oregonfootball fakes a FG and kicker Gage Hurych takes it in himself pic.twitter.com/gpQMsdnJXa — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) November 21, 2026 “We just want to try to find every edge,” Lanning said in his on-field postgame interview with Fox Sports. “When there’s an opportunity to create an edge, we want to be able to find it. Special teams have been game-changers for us this season. It’s a great opportunity to create momentum. If we see it out there, we want to take advantage of it.” Oregon did the same thing at Ohio State on Nov. 7. At the time, the Ducks were trailing 14-3 to a No. 12 Buckeyes squad desperate for a bounce-back victory. Lanning was a facing a fourth-and-9 from his own 31-yard line. Thumbs up for this play call pic.twitter.com/9MgNejGRJh — CBS Sports College Football 🏈 (@CBSSportsCFB) November 7, 2026 He called for a fake punt that saw Teitum Tuioti catch the snap, run forward and then lob a jump pass to fellow outside linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei. The 6-foot-5, 265-pound Uiagalelei barreled down the sideline and capped a momentous 30-yard gain with a hurdle. That drive ended in a touchdown and was a critical part of Oregon scoring 38 straight points in what wound up being a 41-28 win in Columbus . Lanning’s Ducks entered the season with the highest of expectations. Then their campaign for the program’s first-ever national title went sideways. Quarterback Dante Moore suffered a scary concussion at USC . And the Ducks dropped two of their next three games and to 4-3 on the year. Since, they’ve won four in a row. They’re playing free, taking risks and having fun. Along the way, they’ve preserved their College Football Playoff hopes. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers survived a serious scare against the Sacramento Kings , escaping with a narrow 106-104 victory despite struggling to control the glass and protect their lead. Luka Doncic led the way with 25 points and eight assists, while Walker Kessler and Matisse Thybulle were solid on both ends of the floor. However, this was far from a convincing performance from Los Angeles, which allowed Sacramento to collect 44 rebounds and stay within striking distance. The Lakers shot an efficient 50.0% from the field, compared to Sacramento’s 45.6%, but their 30.6% shooting from three-point range left plenty to be desired. Los Angeles also had to overcome a 16-9 disadvantage in offensive rebounds, giving the Kings second chances throughout the night. The difference came at the free-throw line, where the Lakers converted 17 of 22 attempts compared to Sacramento’s nine of 12. Doncic had the biggest scoring night, but this victory was more of a collective survival effort than a dominant showing from the superstar. Here are the player ratings for every Laker who saw the floor. Luka Doncic: B+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 4 REB, 8 AST, 2 STL, 6 TOV, 9-18 FG, 2-9 3-PT FG, 5-6 FT, 36 MIN Doncic finished as the Lakers’ leading scorer and primary playmaker, but this was not his cleanest performance. He shot 50.0% from the field, yet struggled to find his rhythm from beyond the arc, making just two of nine attempts. Six turnovers also gave Sacramento opportunities to capitalize, particularly in a game decided by only two points. Still, Doncic delivered when the Lakers needed offensive production. His eight assists helped keep the offense moving, and his two steals added some defensive value. The 25-point performance was enough to lead Los Angeles to victory, even if the overall efficiency and ball security left room for improvement. item.title: Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Vegas pole despite “ideal” final-lap position
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes left Friday night qualifying at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit with the fastest car on track, yet team principal Toto Wolff still had questions to answer. World champion Kimi Antonelli topped Q3 with a 1m33.893s, only to drop to sixth on the grid due to a five-place penalty for taking Mercedes’ updated ADUO turbocharger. Instead of team-mate George Russell inheriting pole, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen snatched top spot with a 1m34.151s - edging Russell’s 1m34.224s by just 0.073 seconds. The result stung after Russell had looked untouchable earlier in the evening, topping final practice with a 1m34.041s that put him 0.911s clear of Antonelli. Complicating matters in Q3, Russell had asked Mercedes for a slipstream from his already-penalised team-mate. Instead, a messy final out-lap left Antonelli trailing the pack, allowing the Italian to pull a tow worth up to 16 km/h down the Strip straight from cars ahead—including Russell. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes Asked after qualifying whether Mercedes should have orchestrated a better tow to aid Russell’s fight for second in the Drivers’ Championship, Wolff dismissed track positioning as the culprit. "Actually, George for me had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front," Wolff said. "We need to find out because I think there was some kind of Turn 7, 8, 9 - whether there was a mistake or something else happened, I don’t know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap because he was quickest all the time." Setting up front-row “cinema” with Verstappen Even without pole, Russell lines up second alongside Verstappen on Saturday night with major championship stakes on the line. Sitting third in the standings and 17 points behind Verstappen, Russell has a prime chance to make serious ground after both Ferraris - Charles Leclerc (11th) and Lewis Hamilton (12th) - were knocked out in Q2. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes Tension between the front-row rivals is already running hot. Late in FP3, Verstappen and Russell tangled wheel-to-wheel at Turn 14 after Verstappen passed the Mercedes and slowed into the corner, prompting the Dutchman to complain over team radio that Russell had "pushed me into the barrier". Following a post-session review, the FIA stewards handed Verstappen a warning for the skirmish. Asked what he expected when the pair launch side by side toward Turn 1, Wolff didn't downplay the prospect of fireworks. "Well, with cinema, if they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching," Wolff said. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.description: OKLAHOMA CITY — Racing down the floor, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had his eyes set on the rim. He trucked through Jeremiah Fears to bank in the and-one layup. The two-time MVP walked the baseline and stared at the crowd before he finished the dagger three-point play with 34 seconds left. The Oklahoma City Thunder survived a thriller in a 126-120 win over the New Orleans Pelicans . This was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B. In a sport that features plenty of runs, this was one even more roller-coast-esque than usual. The Thunder completely blitzed the Pelicans to get started with a quick 11-0 lead a little over two minutes in. And then New Orleans immediately responded with a 17-4 run. Saddiq Bey buried an outside jumper to cap it off. The Thunder were in a 36-33 deficit after the first quarter. Once again, it was another NBA opponent that completely cooked OKC from the perimeter. This time, it was by one of the worst outside-shooting teams in the league. The second quarter was much the same story. As the Thunder fell behind by double-digit points, they couldn't muster up much offense. Pair that with the Pelicans getting whatever they wanted, it was a recipe for bad vibes. Zion Williamson bully-balled his way to the cup. He looked like his vintage self. Jeremiah Fears' speed helped him dissect OKC's defense. The latter only had 23 points in the second frame. It was in a 64-56 deficit at halftime. Yeesh. The Thunder looked lifeless for most of the first half. For as demoralizing as things have gotten with them, multiply that by 10 for the Pelicans. To finish a putrid first half, Gilgeous-Alexander had a scary-looking fall on a drive to the basket. His shoulder collided with the floor. To start the second half, the Thunder fell into an even deeper hole. Herbert Jones' back-to-back corner 3-pointers were soul-crushers. That put OKC in a 91-76 deficit. The possibility of dropping another gimme stared them straight in the face once again. They salvaged things with a 14-2 run to end the third frame. At that point, the Thunder scored 36 points in the third quarter. The offense finally started to play like an upper-half team. Jared McCain and Bennett Stirtz caught on fire. Aday Mara was a godsend as he played like an old-school seven-footer. They were in a 98-92 deficit with a dozen minutes to go. Another clutch-time scenario was on the verge of materializing. Eventually, McCain erupted the OKC crowd with a game-tying outside jumper. Knotted up at 102 points with nine minutes left, the Thunder played rejuvenated in comparison to their first-half selves. Mara injected some youthful energy as a stop-and-board sequence had him thumping his chest in excitement. When Gilgeous-Alexander checked in, they actually had a three-point lead with eight minutes left — a great spot to be at. item.title: Hopewell football wins instant classic against Propel in WPIAL semifinals
item.description: DORMONT — When the game is on the line and you need a play to win the game, you’re going to call on your best player. That’s exactly the situation that Hopewell found itself in the WPIAL 3A high school football semifinal game against Propel Braddock Hills. After a stop on defense, the team called on junior quarterback and Penn State commit James Armstrong , who took a keeper to the end zone to send the team to the WPIAL championship with a 66-60 double-overtime win on Friday, Nov. 20. “In that situation, nobody is getting the ball other than No. 5 [James Armstrong],” Hopewell interim head coach John Rosa said. “Everyone played great tonight and when you have a Division I quarterback, you put the ball in his hands and let him win you the game.” The semifinal victory for Hopewell will go down as one of the best games in WPIAL playoff history, featuring 126 combined points between the two sides. But it wasn’t a back-and-forth affair throughout, with Hopewell (12-1) having to claw its way back from multiple deficits, including a 16-point hole halfway through the third quarter. After Propel Braddock Hills (8-4) struck for an 11-yard touchdown run by running back Daniel Stephens, Armstrong threw an interception to Mikal Hall, setting up an 85-yard pick-six that — in many games — would have been the nail in the coffin. But not for Hopewell. Following the pick-six, Hopewell answered, with Brody Rock and Avery Bokor combining on a kickoff return, as Rock flipped the ball to Bokor at the Propel 12-yard-line and ran the rest of the way. item.title: No. 8 Pomperaug football rallies past Notre Dame Prep in OT behind Jack Guinipero
item.description: Pomperaug's Caleb McKee (40) goes up to make the game-tying touchdown catch against Notre Dame Prep during a football game at Sacred Heart University on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. (Dave Stewart/Hearst Connecticut Media) FAIRFIELD - The Pomperaug football team has been stomping all over opponents with a relentless rushing attack this season. But senior Jack Guinipero made one thing clear after the team's latest game. "We can pass, too," he said with a laugh. Guinipero threw a game-tying touchdown pass to Caleb McKee with 51 seconds remaining, then ran for an 8-yard score in overtime to give No. 8-ranked Pomperaug a dramatic 27-20 victory over Notre Dame Prep on Friday at Sacred Heart University's Campus Field. Guinipero even had a hand, literally, on the final play when he knocked away a fourth-down pass from Notre Dame Prep's Jordan Razor. But the tying pass, on a play Guinipero called "28 Rocket Pass," was the biggest highlight, with Guinipero firing a pass from the sidelines into the end zone, and McKee going up under double coverage to make the catch. "That's something we've had on the back burner forever," Guinipero said. "It's one of those plays where, we've got it in our back pocket any time we need it. I hit my favorite receiver, Caleb McKee, an absolute dog and he went over two people for it. Beast, I love to see it." While the pass was the highlight, the running game did the heavy lifting as usual, with Guinipero rushing for 119 yards and a touchdown, Dom Creaco rushing for 80 yards and two touchdowns, and Josh Coughlin rushing for 97 yards. But the Panthers had to overcome three turnovers: two fumbles and an interception by Notre Dame Prep's Razor. "What I loved about this was we overcame that," Pomperaug coach Tom Pereira said. "We kept fighting and fighting, held them out for a two (point attempt) to keep the game within reach, and then we made plays down the stretch. I challenged our defense before this game. Aside from that series coming out of the halftime, we really bottled up their running game and forced them to have to go vertically down the field." The game was the regular-season finale for both teams, which had already unofficially secured playoff berths. Pomperaug (9-1) will be making its first trip to the state tournament since finishing runner-up in the Class L championship in 2009. The Panthers are currently second in Class MM and will likely host a quarterfinal game. Notre Dame Prep (8-2), which is in Class M, is back in the playoffs after missing the cut last season, but Friday's loss may have cost it a shot at a home playoff game. The Lancers are now sixth in Class M. "Going into the playoffs, this is the type of game you want," Notre Dame Prep coach John Johnson said. item.description: Berlin's Gamaliel Ayizano, 4, blasts through the line during the CIAC football game between Middletown and Berlin high schools.Friday, November 20, 2026, Sage Park, Berlin, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) Two more high school football teams unofficially clinched CIAC playoff spots Friday night, according to GametimeCT calculations, bringing the statewide total to 28 (out of 48) as Week 11 nears its conclusion this weekend. BERLIN (7-3) , last year's Class M champion, clinched a spot in Class SS thanks to its 35-32 victory over rival Middletown at Sage Park. GRANBY/CANTON (8-2) defeated CREC, 41-6 at New Britain, to earn a spot in Class S. They join DANBURY (5-4) , which managed to clinch a spot in Class LL on Thursday afternoon when St. Joseph defeated Westhill, 57-3. Simsbury (8-2) had a chance at clinching a spot in Class L, but concluded its regular season with a 56-28 loss to Glastonbury (3-7). The Trojans (8-2), however, have a favorable path to the playoff based on outside results in the coming days. Middletown (7-3) would have clinched a spot in Class MM had it defeated Berlin, but now must wait for outside results. The CIAC playoff qualifier projections are determined using the CIAC playoff formula , using OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna medium model and verified by GametimeCT using the current CIAC football playoff standings and formula. All qualifiers remain unofficial until the CIAC's football committee meets the day after the regular season concludes on Thanksgiving morning. The playoffs begin Tuesday, Dec. 1 at the sites of the top-four seeds in each of the six divisions. Elsewhere, New Britain (8-2) concluded its regular season with a 24-19 victory over West Haven, a win that clinched one of the top four seeds in Class LL and a home playoff game for the quarterfinals. Pomperaug (9-1) also clinched at least a home quarterfinal in Class MM when it defeated Notre Dame Prep 27-20 in overtime. At least one more playoff spot can be secured Saturday when Bloomfield plays host to Windsor. A win will clinch a Class S spot for the Warhawks. Windsor, last year's Class MM champion, needs a win to keep its faint hopes at defending that title alive. item.title: JJ Redick Gives Two Reasons For Replacing Jake LaRavia With Ziaire Williams On Lakers’ Starting Lineup
item.description: Nov 9, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick reacts on the sidelines during the game against the Atlanta Hawks at State Farm Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers play the Sacramento Kings tonight at the Crypto.Com Arena. Head coach JJ Redick once again replaced Jake LaRavia with Ziaire Williams in the Lakers’ starting lineup. Ahead of tonight’s game, JJ Redick spoke to the media and explained the decision that initially puzzled many Lakers fans when they made it in their 97-109 loss to the Jazz, which ended their nine-game winning streak. “I felt like, with the group they were going to start, again, we talked to Ziaire and Jake when we were in Milwaukee last week about both of those guys having some flexibility.” “I think Ziaire was in a really good rhythm, and he’s had some good games since he missed some time. We were trying to get him back into a rhythm. He hasn’t really had one over the last three games or so. So, some of it was about that, and some of it was about the matchup.” “Those guys are both easy, low-maintenance winners. They’re not going to be affected by that. I think the message from day one of training camp has always been that every game is going to be a little different. It’s going to present itself differently, and the challenges are going to be different. You have to play the game in front of you, and the guys are bought into that,” Redick explained . Before tonight, Jake LaRavia averaged 5.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 2.2 assists while shooting 47.1% from the field and 46.7% from beyond the arc so far this season. Ziaire Williams averaged 9.5 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 1.8 assists while shooting 56.4% from the field and 44.7% from beyond the arc. It seemed like Jake LaRavia had cemented his role in the Lakers’ starting lineup in 15 games (11 starts). But Ziaire Williams clearly stepped up and made a promising case for a starter role (six starts in 13 games played). The Lakers began the season with three prominently fixed starters whenever they are healthy: Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler. As a result, the wings were always a position to contend for and earn as the season progressed. Given that both power forwards are willing to do whatever it takes to win, this is a good problem for the Lakers: everyone plays so well that they don’t know who to start or who can come off the bench and make an impact. They seem likely to use this position rotationally throughout the season, based on the matchups they expect. It will be interesting to see who the Lakers’ coaching staff decides to start as the playoffs approach later in the season. But down the stretch, it remains to be seen who earns the regular starting power-forward role, as role clarity helps players mold their tendencies accordingly.

item.title: Antonelli fastest but penalty leaves Verstappen on pole
item.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. "I wanted to be on pole but I am probably more pleased with the performance than in Mexico when I was on the front row. "Kimi did a great job and he probably thought it wasn't going to work out so well being so close but with the tow it worked out." Top 10 1. Cleveland sits just behind the Miami Heat in NBA Cup Group Stage play, while the Pacers fall to 1-2. Harden finished 15-26 from the floor, including 7 for 11 from beyond the arc, to go with six assists and six rebounds. Oh, and in classic fashion, he was also 14-14 from the free throw line. Cleveland now sits just over .500 at 9-8, beating an Indiana team that was still without star guard Tyrese Haliburton. The Cavs did not have forward Evan Mobley, who is undergoing treatment for a great toe sprain. Peyton Watson returned from a one-game absence due to a back injury, and provided 15 points, four rebounds, and three assists. The two teams were neck and neck in the first half, with the Cavs holding a slight one-point advantage at the break. But it was the 37-year-old Harden who took over in the third quarter, helping Cleveland outscore Indiana 43-23 in the frame. Harden’s 51-point effort, the 26th of his career, puts him past Kobe Bryant for third on the NBA’s all-time 50-point game list. “My idol, the person I watched growing up,” Harden said in a postgame interview when told he passed Bryant on the all-time list. Harden has been playing much better of late following his slow start, something that the former MVP has built into his conditioning strategy of playing into game shape. Mitchell’s 20 points mostly came in the second half, but he helped apply pressure in that “Cavalanche” of a third quarter that allowed Cleveland to pull away. item.title: Clemson commit drills 58-yard field goal, walk-off winner in Florida playoff stunner
item.description: Brandin Gallaway has the leg to change a football game. Friday night, the Clemson commit did it twice . The Palmetto senior kicker drilled a 58-yard field goal to tie the game before halftime, then came through with a 34-yard kick as time expired to give the Tigers a dramatic 12-10 upset of Tampa Bay Tech in the Class 5A-Region 3 semifinals . Gallaway accounted for all 12 of Palmetto's points, converting all four of his field-goal attempts to send the Tigers (11-1) into the regional final. His biggest kick of the first half came with 35 seconds remaining. Facing a long attempt, Gallaway connected from 58 yards to tie the game at 6-6 and give Palmetto momentum heading into the break. Tampa Bay Tech had taken the lead late in the first quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Martavius Conway Jr., but missed the extra point. Gallaway put Palmetto ahead with a 42-yard field goal with 3:41 remaining in the third quarter. Tampa Bay Tech answered with a 29-yard field goal with four minutes left in the game, setting up a dramatic finish. The Tigers' ensuing possession stalled near midfield, but their defense gave Gallaway another opportunity. Palmetto's defense flushed Conway out of the pocket, and Jordan Allen stepped in front of his pass at the Tampa Bay Tech 42-yard line, returning the interception to the 34. Palmetto moved the ball to the 17-yard line before sending Gallaway onto the field with three seconds remaining. The senior, like he had all night, delivered once more for safe measure. His 34-yard attempt sailed through the uprights as time expired, sending Palmetto into the regional final and capping a four-field-goal performance that will be difficult to forget. Palmetto will travel to face top-seeded Armwood next Friday. Armwood advanced with a 37-12 victory over Sumner. item.title: Rangers Acquire Max Sasson From Canucks To Fill Bottom-Six Center Role
item.description: Bob Frid-Imagn Images The New York Rangers acquired Max Sasson from the Vancouver Canucks on Friday in exchange for a 2029 fourth-round pick. After losing Joe Veleno due to a lower-body injury on Oct. 4 after just four regular-season games, the Rangers have been searching for another bottom-six center, with a rotating cast of centers filling in Veleno’s spot on the fourth line. Sasson fits the criteria the Rangers are looking for. Over his three seasons with the Canucks, Sasson has recorded 21 goals, 13 assists, and 34 points in 119 games while averaging 11:27 minutes. The 26-year-old center has experience as a penalty killer and provides an element of speed to the Rangers’ bottom-six forward unit. During the offseason, the Rangers signed Veleno to a one-year, $1.2 million contract, and he helped balance out the lineup during his four games before landing on injured reserve, as he took on important defensive responsibilities. Veleno resumed skating on his own on Friday, which Sullivan views as a step in the right direction. item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen will start on pole at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix despite Kimi Antonelli going fastest - while Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton both failed to make Q3. The 2026 world champion beat the Red Bull driver by 0.258s, but will take a five-place grid drop due to a new internal combustion engine on his Mercedes. It came after Verstappen took provisional pole with a 1m34.151s while Antonelli was down in sixth, but the Dutchman failed to improve on his final lap, allowing others the chance to beat him. Yet only Antonelli managed to topple Verstappen, setting a 1m33.893s at the chequered flag - the eighth time he has gone quickest in qualifying this year and the first since Austin. But because of the grid penalty, Verstappen will be joined on the front row by Mercedes’ George Russell, who hoped for a tow from his team-mate but traffic denied that opportunity. Russell set a 1m34.224s, two-tenths quicker than his opening lap, and was just 0.020s ahead of McLaren’s Lando Norris, who will therefore complete the top three on Saturday night’s grid. Verstappen’s team-mate Isack Hadjar was fifth quickest in Q3, 0.699s off the pace, with sixth going to impressive rookie Arivd Lindblad a week after Racing Bulls confirmed him for 2027. Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Oscar Piastri took seventh, but is one of five drivers set for a grid penalty, his being 10 places for an engine change, while eighth went to Lindblad’s team-mate Liam Lawson. Alpine duo Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto respectively completed the top 10, 1.212s and 1.421s off Antonelli, but the biggest talking point came in the second session as Ferrari suffered its first double Q2 exit since Imola last year. The Italian outfit occupied row six after what was a messy Q2, highlighted by Leclerc aborting a lap midway through due to a Turn 7 lock-up. The Monegasque subsequently failed to make the line to start a lap at the end, eventually dropping to 11th ahead of 12th-placed Hamilton, who failed to improve on his final tour. “Unbelievable,” reacted Leclerc, whose team-mate would have knocked out Antonelli had he improved at the chequered flag - the Italian surviving the drop by 0.111s. Three-tenths behind Hamilton was Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg in 13th, with 14th going to Williams man Carlos Sainz, who is set to serve a 10-place drop for a new turbocharger. Hulkenberg’s team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto will jump up from 15th, while 16th went to Alex Albon for Williams’ first double Q2 appearance of the 2026 season. Rafael Camara, who suffered a spin at the opening corner early on, looked set to profit from a significant tow by team-mate Oliver Bearman until Bortoleto dropped him into the Q1 elimination zone at the chequered flag. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
